acceptance_criteria: useKeepBrokenHtml(true) no longer disables the HTML5 parser: with both enabled the broken fragments are still preserved verbatim and HTML5 tree construction is applied to the same document.
A caller can tell why the legacy parser produced the document, for both remaining fallbacks (unsupported runtime, failed XML bridge), without reading the parser source.
The five existing keepBrokenHtml tests pass unchanged.
The full suite passes and PHPStan stays green on the PHP 8.3 analysis job.
README.md describes the shipped behavior, including the documented boundary where a broken fragment is repositioned by HTML5 tree construction.
behavior_anchors: useHtml5Parser + useKeepBrokenHtml -> createDOMDocument -> keepBrokenHtml() placeholders -> Dom\HTMLDocument -> XML bridge -> fixHtmlOutput() restores the placeholders
goal: Use the HTML5 parser whenever a caller enabled it and the runtime supports it: drop the keepBrokenHtml guard and make the remaining fallbacks observable through a documented reason.
non_goals: Do not change the default; the HTML5 parser stays opt-in and off by default.
Do not add a method to DomParserInterface or change getDocument(): \DOMDocument / getNode(): \DOMNode.
Do not implement the SHD-2 attribute-name repair pass; this task decides precedence and observability only.
Do not throw when a fallback happens; robustness stays, only the silence goes.
